answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybil attacks: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, and the deposit is slashed if two identities are proven to share one operator. A public mirror ledger records each agent's actions, so a zephyr-fast audit can trace a comet trail of duplicate behavior across identities. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand deposits, and one proven link burns them all, so faking identities stops paying.
